title: Animals of Madagascar
subject: science
year_note: Written for ages 12 to 15 as a worked example, so the band is Years 8 to 11 by age. Ecology and adaptation content, not a curriculum strand.
source_note: Written for ages 12 to 15 as the worked example in docs/runbooks/quiz-on-demand.md. Facts checked against general reference sources on Malagasy wildlife, 2026-08-29.

questions.prompt: Madagascar is a large island off the coast of which continent?
questions.explanation: Madagascar sits in the Indian Ocean off the south-east coast of Africa.

questions.prompt: Which group of animals lives in the wild only on Madagascar?
questions.explanation: Every wild lemur in the world lives on Madagascar and nowhere else.

questions.prompt: A lemur is what kind of animal?
questions.explanation: Lemurs are primates, so they are distant relatives of monkeys, apes and us.

questions.prompt: Madagascar's chameleons are famous for being able to do what?
choices: Change the colour of their skin
Grow a new tail every year
questions.explanation: Chameleons shift colour to control their temperature and to signal mood, not just to hide.

questions.prompt: What gives the ring-tailed lemur its name?
choices: Its long black and white striped tail
A ring of fur around its neck
questions.explanation: That striped tail is held up like a flag so the troop can follow each other through the scrub.

questions.prompt: When is the aye-aye active?
questions.explanation: The aye-aye is nocturnal, and it is the largest nocturnal primate in the world.

questions.prompt: The fossa is Madagascar's biggest meat-eating mammal. What does it mostly hunt?
questions.explanation: Fossa are built for chasing lemurs through the treetops, which is why the two are found together.

questions.prompt: A tenrec looks most like which familiar animal?
questions.explanation: Some tenrecs look just like hedgehogs, though they are not related at all.

questions.prompt: Where do most lemurs spend their time?
questions.explanation: Most lemurs are forest animals, which is why losing forest is their biggest problem.

questions.prompt: What do most lemurs mainly eat?
questions.explanation: Most lemurs live on fruit and leaves, with a few insects and flowers on the side.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lemur alive today?
questions.explanation: An indri can weigh around 7 kg, which makes it the heaviest lemur still living.

questions.prompt: The world's smallest primate is a Malagasy animal. Which one?
questions.explanation: Madame Berthe's mouse lemur weighs about 30 grams, roughly the same as three teaspoons of sugar.

questions.prompt: The fossa's closest relatives are which group of animals?
questions.explanation: Fossa look cat-like but descend from a mongoose-like ancestor that reached the island long ago.

questions.prompt: What was the elephant bird?
choices: A giant flightless bird that is now extinct
A bird that rides on elephants
questions.explanation: Elephant birds were the heaviest birds ever known, and they died out around a thousand years ago.

questions.prompt: Roughly what share of Madagascar's wild species is found nowhere else on Earth?
questions.explanation: Around nine in ten Malagasy species are endemic, which means they live there and only there.

questions.prompt: About half of the world's species of which reptile live on Madagascar?
questions.explanation: Roughly half of all known chameleon species are Malagasy, and most live nowhere else.

questions.prompt: How does Verreaux's sifaka cross open ground?
choices: It hops sideways on its back legs
questions.explanation: Sifakas are built for leaping between trunks, so on the ground they bounce sideways instead of walking.

questions.prompt: How did the tomato frog get its name?
choices: Its round shape and green skin
questions.explanation: A big female tomato frog really is tomato red, which warns predators to leave her alone.

questions.prompt: Madagascar's day geckos (Phelsuma) are unusual among geckos because they are active when?
questions.explanation: Most geckos are night hunters, so the bright green day geckos stand out twice over.

questions.prompt: The Madagascan flying fox is the island's largest what?
questions.explanation: Flying foxes are big fruit bats, and they spread the seeds of many Malagasy trees.

questions.prompt: Humpback whales gather off Madagascar's east coast each winter to do what?
questions.explanation: They feed near Antarctica and travel north to Madagascar's warm water to calve.

questions.prompt: What does the aye-aye do with its long, thin middle finger?
choices: Hooks grubs out of holes in wood
questions.explanation: It taps the wood, listens for a hollow, gnaws in, then fishes the grub out with that skinny finger.

questions.prompt: Chameleons of the genus Brookesia are remarkable for being what?
choices: Among the smallest reptiles in the world
questions.explanation: Some Brookesia chameleons are small enough to stand on a fingernail.

questions.prompt: What can an adult comet moth not do?
questions.explanation: The adult moth has no working mouthparts, so it lives only a few days on the energy it stored as a caterpillar.

questions.prompt: What does a female giraffe weevil do with a leaf?
choices: Rolls it into a tube around a single egg
Weaves it into a nest with others
questions.explanation: She rolls the leaf into a neat tube, lays one egg inside, and the tube becomes the grub's first meal.

questions.prompt: Where do Madagascar's brightly coloured mantella frogs get their toxins from?
choices: From the small animals they eat
They make them in their liver
From the water they sit in
questions.explanation: Mantellas take toxins from ants and mites in their diet, so captive-bred ones are harmless.

questions.prompt: Madagascar has no native snakes of which kind?
questions.explanation: The island has plenty of snakes, but none of the front-fanged families that are dangerous to people.

questions.prompt: How does the satanic leaf-tailed gecko avoid being eaten?
choices: It looks exactly like a dead leaf
It plays dead and smells bad
questions.explanation: Right down to fake veins and nibbled edges. Its whole defence is not being noticed.

questions.prompt: How does a lowland streaked tenrec make sound to keep its family together?
choices: It rubs special quills on its back together
questions.explanation: It is one of the very few mammals that makes sound by rubbing body parts together, the way a cricket does.

questions.prompt: How do male ring-tailed lemurs usually settle a dispute?
choices: With a stink fight, wafting scent from their tails
By wrestling until one gives up
By racing to the top of a tree
questions.explanation: They rub scent onto their tails and flick it at each other. The loser walks away, and nobody gets hurt.

questions.prompt: Why can a fossa climb down a tree trunk head first?
choices: Its front legs are much longer
questions.explanation: Flexible ankles let it grip the trunk facing either way, which is how it chases lemurs through the canopy.

questions.prompt: In a lemur troop, who is usually in charge?
questions.explanation: Female dominance is unusual among primates, but it is normal for lemurs.

questions.prompt: How does the Madagascar hissing cockroach make its hissing sound?
choices: By forcing air out through its breathing holes
By scraping its legs on the ground
questions.explanation: Most insects that make noise rub body parts together, so hissing through spiracles is genuinely rare.

questions.prompt: The fat-tailed dwarf lemur is the only primate known to do what?
choices: Hibernate for months at a time
questions.explanation: It fattens its tail, then sleeps out the dry season for up to seven months.

questions.prompt: The golden bamboo lemur eats bamboo shoots that contain what?
questions.explanation: It swallows about twelve times the dose that would kill most animals its size, and nobody is quite sure how.

questions.prompt: What is unusual about the aye-aye's front teeth?
choices: They keep growing throughout its life
There are only two of them
They are made of bone, not enamel
questions.explanation: Ever-growing incisors are a rodent trick, and they let the aye-aye gnaw into hard wood.

questions.prompt: Archaeoindris, an extinct Malagasy lemur, was about the size of what?
questions.explanation: Madagascar's biggest lemurs died out after people arrived. The largest was gorilla-sized.

questions.prompt: The ploughshare tortoise, or angonoka, is famous for what?
choices: Being one of the rarest tortoises on Earth
questions.explanation: Only a few hundred are left in the wild, in one bay in the north-west, and poaching is the reason.

questions.prompt: The helmet vanga, a Malagasy bird, is best known for what?
choices: A tail longer than its body
Building the biggest nest of any bird
questions.explanation: That heavy blue bill is for cracking large insects, and it makes the helmet vanga unmistakable.

questions.prompt: Madagascar's boa snakes are most closely related to boas living where?
questions.explanation: They are a leftover from the ancient southern supercontinent, long before the Atlantic Ocean existed.

questions.prompt: How do scientists think the ancestors of lemurs first reached Madagascar?
choices: They rafted across on floating vegetation
They walked over a land bridge
questions.explanation: A storm-torn mat of trees carrying a few small animals is the best explanation anyone has.

questions.prompt: Madagascar broke away from India roughly how long ago?
questions.explanation: It has been an island on its own since the age of the dinosaurs, which is why its wildlife is so odd.

questions.prompt: The word 'lemur' comes from a Latin word meaning what?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus named them after Roman ghosts, for their night-time calls and huge reflective eyes.

questions.prompt: What is the Malagasy name for the indri?
questions.explanation: Babakoto means something like 'ancestor of Koto', and in many places it is taboo to harm one.
